# Resource: stripe_treasury_outbound_transfer

A transfer of money out of a Treasury financial account to another financial account of the same connected account, given with `destination_payment_method_data`, or to a US bank account attached to the connected account itself, which `destination_payment_method` names. Treasury runs on a platform's connected accounts, so manage outbound transfers through a provider configuration whose `stripe_account` is the connected account. The financial account needs its `intra_stripe_flows` feature active to send to a financial account, and `outbound_transfers.ach` to send to a bank account. See `stripe_treasury_inbound_transfer` for how a bank account is attached. Stripe posts a transfer to a financial account at once, and one to a bank account within about a second, and `status` then reads `posted`. Set `status` to `canceled` to cancel a transfer that is still `processing` and that Stripe reports `cancelable`. Stripe refuses to cancel one that has posted: a plan that sets `canceled` then fails, and an apply that finds the transfer posted fails with Stripe's answer. Nothing else changes after creation.

~> A treasury outbound transfer can move real money. In a live-mode Stripe account, creating or changing one, including setting its `status`, fails at plan time unless the provider sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. Reading or importing one never does. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode. See the Managing Test Data guide.

~> Stripe cannot delete an outbound transfer; set `status` to `canceled` to cancel one that is still processing. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the treasury outbound transfer, fail at plan time. To stop managing a treasury outbound transfer, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "treasury_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "A connected account with the treasury capability active."
}

variable "financial_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "A financial account of the connected account."
}

# Treasury runs on a connected account, so a second provider configuration acts on it.
provider "stripe" {
  alias          = "treasury"
  stripe_account = var.treasury_account
}

variable "savings_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "Another financial account of the same connected account."
}

resource "stripe_treasury_outbound_transfer" "to_savings" {
  provider          = stripe.treasury
  financial_account = var.financial_account
  amount            = 5000
  currency          = "usd"

  destination_payment_method_data = {
    type              = "financial_account"
    financial_account = var.savings_account
  }
}

# Stripe posts a transfer between financial accounts at once.
output "outbound_transfer_status" {
  value = stripe_treasury_outbound_transfer.to_savings.status
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `amount` - (Required) Amount (in cents) to be transferred. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `currency` - (Required) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `financial_account` - (Required) The FinancialAccount to pull funds from. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

The following arguments are optional:

* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `destination_payment_method` - (Optional) The PaymentMethod to use as the payment instrument for the OutboundTransfer. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `destination_payment_method_data` - (Optional) Hash used to generate the PaymentMethod to be used for this OutboundTransfer. Exclusive with `destination_payment_method`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`destination_payment_method_data`](#destination_payment_method_data) below.
* `destination_payment_method_options` - (Optional) Hash describing payment method configuration details. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`destination_payment_method_options`](#destination_payment_method_options) below.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `statement_descriptor` - (Optional) Statement descriptor to be shown on the receiving end of an OutboundTransfer. Maximum 10 characters for `ach` transfers or 140 characters for `us_domestic_wire` transfers. The default value is "transfer". Can only include -#.$&*, spaces, and alphanumeric characters. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `status` - (Optional) Current status of the OutboundTransfer: `processing`, `failed`, `canceled`, `posted`, `returned`. An OutboundTransfer is `processing` if it has been created and is pending. The status changes to `posted` once the OutboundTransfer has been "confirmed" and funds have left the account, or to `failed` or `canceled`. If an OutboundTransfer fails to arrive at its destination, its status will change to `returned`. Possible values: `canceled`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

### `destination_payment_method_data`

The `destination_payment_method_data` attribute supports:

* `financial_account` - (Optional)
* `type` - (Required) Possible values: `financial_account`.

<a id="destination_payment_method_options"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_options`

The `destination_payment_method_options` attribute supports:

* `us_bank_account` - (Optional) See [`destination_payment_method_options.us_bank_account`](#destination_payment_method_options.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="destination_payment_method_options.us_bank_account"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_options.us_bank_account`

The `destination_payment_method_options.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `network` - (Optional) Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `cancelable` - Returns `true` if the object can be canceled, and `false` otherwise.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `destination_payment_method_details` - See [`destination_payment_method_details`](#destination_payment_method_details) below.
* `expected_arrival_date` - The date when funds are expected to arrive in the destination account.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `returned_details` - Details about a returned OutboundTransfer. Only set when the status is `returned`. See [`returned_details`](#returned_details) below.
* `status_transitions` - See [`status_transitions`](#status_transitions) below.
* `tracking_details` - Details about network-specific tracking information if available. See [`tracking_details`](#tracking_details) below.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="destination_payment_method_details"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_details`

The `destination_payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `billing_details` - See [`destination_payment_method_details.billing_details`](#destination_payment_method_details.billing_details) below.
* `financial_account` - See [`destination_payment_method_details.financial_account`](#destination_payment_method_details.financial_account) below.
* `type` - The type of the payment method used in the OutboundTransfer. Possible values: `financial_account`, `us_bank_account`.
* `us_bank_account` - See [`destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`](#destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="destination_payment_method_details.billing_details"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_details.billing_details`

The `destination_payment_method_details.billing_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - See [`destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`](#destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address) below.
* `email` - Email address.
* `name` - Full name.

<a id="destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`

The `destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="destination_payment_method_details.financial_account"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_details.financial_account`

The `destination_payment_method_details.financial_account` attribute supports:

* `id` - Token of the FinancialAccount.
* `network` - The rails used to send funds. Possible values: `stripe`.

<a id="destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - Account holder type: individual or company. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `account_type` - Account type: checkings or savings. Defaults to checking if omitted. Possible values: `checking`, `savings`.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `network` - The network rails used. See the [docs](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/money-movement/timelines) to learn more about money movement timelines for each network type. Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.
* `routing_number` - Routing number of the bank account.

<a id="returned_details"></a>
### `returned_details`

The `returned_details` attribute supports:

* `code` - Reason for the return. Possible values: `account_closed`, `account_frozen`, `bank_account_restricted`, `bank_ownership_changed`, `declined`, `incorrect_account_holder_name`, `invalid_account_number`, `invalid_currency`, `no_account`, `other`.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="status_transitions"></a>
### `status_transitions`

The `status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `canceled_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `canceled`
* `failed_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `failed`
* `posted_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `posted`
* `returned_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `returned`

<a id="tracking_details"></a>
### `tracking_details`

The `tracking_details` attribute supports:

* `ach` - See [`tracking_details.ach`](#tracking_details.ach) below.
* `type` - The US bank account network used to send funds. Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.
* `us_domestic_wire` - See [`tracking_details.us_domestic_wire`](#tracking_details.us_domestic_wire) below.

<a id="tracking_details.ach"></a>
### `tracking_details.ach`

The `tracking_details.ach` attribute supports:

* `trace_id` - ACH trace ID of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `ach` network.

<a id="tracking_details.us_domestic_wire"></a>
### `tracking_details.us_domestic_wire`

The `tracking_details.us_domestic_wire` attribute supports:

* `chips` - CHIPS System Sequence Number (SSN) of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.
* `imad` - IMAD of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.
* `omad` - OMAD of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.

## Removing from State

To stop managing a treasury outbound transfer whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_treasury_outbound_transfer.to_savings

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_treasury_outbound_transfer.to_savings
```

The treasury outbound transfer stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

Run the import where the resource's `provider` acts on the connected account that holds it.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a treasury outbound transfer using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_treasury_outbound_transfer.to_savings
  id = "obt_1MtX4wLkdIwHu7ixK8QwIuNj"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_treasury_outbound_transfer.to_savings
  identity = {
    id = "obt_1MtX4wLkdIwHu7ixK8QwIuNj"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the treasury outbound transfer.

Using `terraform import`, import a treasury outbound transfer using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_treasury_outbound_transfer.to_savings obt_1MtX4wLkdIwHu7ixK8QwIuNj
```

~> Stripe does not return `destination_payment_method_data` or `destination_payment_method_options`, so an imported transfer has neither in state. Add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [destination_payment_method_data, destination_payment_method_options] }` to a configuration that sets them, because a plan that changes them fails.
